items.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object moving at constant speed in a straight line can be in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about upward/downward and left/right forces.
items.evidence_job: Navigate a connected equilibrium stimulus by connecting a motion description to a balanced-force representation and identifying which later reasoning depends on earlier conclusions.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text:
A baggage cart travels east in a straight line at a constant 2.0 m/s. Its force model is:

           250 N support ↑
  40 N ←     [cart]     → 40 N
           250 N weight ↓

(a) Is this static or dynamic equilibrium? Explain using the motion description.
(b) Show that the diagram satisfies the equilibrium rule on both axes.
(c) Which conclusion from (b) is needed to explain why the cart can keep moving even though it is in equilibrium?
(d) If the eastward force rises to 55 N while the westward force remains 40 N, determine the new horizontal net force and predict how the motion changes.
items.student_html:
A baggage cart travels east in a straight line at a constant 2.0 m/s. Its force model is:

250 N support ↑
40 N ← [cart] → 40 N
250 N weight ↓

(a) Is this static or dynamic equilibrium? Explain using the motion description.
(b) Show that the diagram satisfies the equilibrium rule on both axes.
(c) Which conclusion from (b) is needed to explain why the cart can keep moving even though it is in equilibrium?
(d) If the eastward force rises to 55 N while the westward force remains 40 N, determine the new horizontal net force and predict how the motion changes.
items.answer: (a) Dynamic equilibrium because the cart moves with constant velocity. (b) Vertical: 250 − 250 = 0 N; horizontal: 40 − 40 = 0 N. (c) Zero net force means velocity can remain constant; equilibrium does not require rest. (d) 15 N east; the velocity begins changing eastward.
items.solution_text: The equilibrium rule is ΣF = 0. A moving object can satisfy it when its velocity is constant. Once the eastward and westward forces are unequal, equilibrium ends and the velocity changes in the direction of the net force.
items.solution_html: The equilibrium rule is ΣF = 0. A moving object can satisfy it when its velocity is constant. Once the eastward and westward forces are unequal, equilibrium ends and the velocity changes in the direction of the net force.

items.student_html: A 65 N laptop rests on a desk. Draw the force diagram and explain why ‘at rest’ does not mean ‘no forces.’

items.student_text: A cart moves right at constant speed with 28 N right and 28 N left. If the rightward force increases to 40 N while the leftward force stays 28 N, predict the change in motion and justify.
items.student_html: A cart moves right at constant speed with 28 N right and 28 N left. If the rightward force increases to 40 N while the leftward force stays 28 N, predict the change in motion and justify.
items.answer: The cart’s velocity begins changing to the right because the new net force is 12 N right.
items.solution_text: Initially the forces balance. After the change, F_net = 40 − 28 = 12 N right, so the velocity cannot remain constant.
items.solution_html: Initially the forces balance. After the change, F_net = 40 − 28 = 12 N right, so the velocity cannot remain constant.

items.student_text: A sled moves left at constant speed with balanced horizontal forces. Then the leftward pull becomes 9 N larger than the rightward resistance. What happens to the velocity?
items.student_html: A sled moves left at constant speed with balanced horizontal forces. Then the leftward pull becomes 9 N larger than the rightward resistance. What happens to the velocity?
items.answer: The velocity changes toward the left.
items.solution_text: A 9 N leftward net force breaks equilibrium, so the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
